issues.message: Not yet placed by a builder GameTest: melon, pumpkin, cake.
Only 48 blocks: too bare for a common (at least 50). Carlton wants more detail, not less.

visual.summary: Adds pumpkins, melons, hay, cake and lanterns: now it reads as a market stall.
problems: The canopy is two full layers of solid blue and light-blue wool, bigger and heavier than the stall under it: from every view the stall is a bright blue box. Make the awning one block thick (or wool on the front edge and carpet/trapdoors behind), sloping down to the front
Colours: the saturated blue/cyan clashes with the medieval palette of every other structure. Use red and white like the butcher's awning, or brown/white, yellow/white
The counter and goods sit deep under the canopy and are half hidden; push the goods to the front edge so they show

visual.summary: Adds a deeper front awning, pumpkins, melons, hay and lanterns at the counter corners.
problems: Round 1 fixes are in: red and white stripes instead of neon blue, and the front awning is one layer stepping down from the back. Still a little heavy: the back canopy is wool on a full plank layer (two blocks thick); a single layer would look lighter. Not blocking.

notes.roof: The new red/white wool valance at the front edge (z0, y2) is the one heavier part; it is only one block deep and hangs in front of the thin awning, so it reads as a market stall valance rather than a thick roof.

notes.levels: Clearly new over L1: the striped front valance, two hanging lanterns, a pumpkin out at the front (x5 z0) and a melon beside the stall.

visual.summary: Level 2 dresses the stall for trading: a striped wool valance along the front, two hanging lanterns, and produce (pumpkin at the front edge, melon at the side, more grain). Goods sit at the counter front as asked.
